The two above-line equivalences replacements and the small de insertion are not counted as main baselines. The single display (144), the two-row square (145), manuscript page 50 and pale foliation 101 are recorded separately.

changes.place: Short graph term on prose baseline 4
changes.ink: The low connected m is followed by a separate dark stop, then graphes with a looped descending g, tall h and final es. The complete short term is readable. Sommes is also legible, but the matching H candidate is not itself counted as an error.
Both sides of the phrase have paired raised short pen strokes. The writer does not draw guillemets. The internal hyphen is visible and is retained.
The sign has three separately traceable strokes: an upper wave, a second wave, and a straight lower bar. It is neither one wave over one bar nor one wave over two straight bars.

changes.place: Left boundary of the right-hand subscript in (144)
changes.ink: No separate opening parenthesis can be traced before the heavily reworked first letter. Its looped strokes are retained as a local g/G uncertainty; an additional delimiter is not supplied. This row concerns only the absent opening delimiter, not a settled choice of g or G.

changes.place: Right boundary of the right-hand subscript in (144)
changes.ink: A clear curved closing parenthesis follows the hatted I-alpha term. It is separate from the raised cancelled group at its upper right. The sole written closing delimiter is preserved even though no separate opening one is visible.

changes.place: Inserted word after compte, prose baseline 9
changes.ink: The small above-line group consists of a looped d and a low outgoing e-stroke. It attaches after compte and before the opening parenthesis. There is no apostrophe or separate ailleurs sequence.

changes.place: Parenthesis enclosing et redonne and its adverb
changes.ink: A large opening curve lies before the live et. The lower portion of the corresponding closing curve is visible at the right sheet edge after the compressed adverb. Les starts the next baseline outside the parenthesis. This row records the delimiters; the adverb is treated separately.

The word begins auto- and continues through matiq with the descending q visible. There is no initial taut- or the long logiquement sequence. At the sheet edge the short ending resembles a small raised t; the short-form/full-form alternatives remain unresolved, so the row is not counted against C.

changes.place: Abbreviation before pour les normalisés, prose baseline 12
changes.ink: The short group consists of i, a compact s/o sequence and a distinct terminal point. No additional m strokes occur between o and the point.

changes.place: Parenthetic adjective after final normalisés, prose baseline 16
changes.ink: The two tall t-strokes, compact au group and final crossed x are visible. The word ends at x before the closing parenthesis; no lement sequence follows.
The pale numeral group has a long upright 1, a central oval 0 and another long upright 1, each distinguishable at the lower-left edge.

decisions.ink: The full display shows two independent wavy strokes over one straight bar. This is the three-stroke approxeq form, not either supplied candidate.

The first subscript position contains a dense upper loop and a long descending loop, with overlapping strokes that do not establish a final g/G choice or a recoverable old/new order. Alpha, the comma, hatted I-alpha and the closing parenthesis are separately readable. No separate opening parenthesis is traceable.

Both G objects and the source prime are clear. The short single connector has a tiny downward terminal at the right, without a secure complete arrowhead. Dash versus a downward half-head remains open.
Strict is readable. A very small terminal group lies just after the final t, but it cannot securely be distinguished as an independent final s rather than the outgoing end of the t-stroke.

notes: Image-view status: page.jpg was opened once and visually read for layout; top.jpg and bottom.jpg were each opened once and read line by line at their supplied native resolution. All eight saved crops were subsequently opened with view_image and actually inspected. No scan102 crop remains unviewed.

The original is 1693 by 2362 pixels. Crop boxes in original coordinates are opening-revision [300,25,1693,250], multi-graphs [300,248,1665,590], formula144 [290,785,1675,1070], compte-equivalences [310,1045,1693,1305], iso-normalises [310,1390,1668,1655], square145 [280,1645,1060,1940], final-paragraph [300,1935,1685,2245], and folio101 [20,2290,125,2352]. Each path is crops/147_scan102_<name>.png. All used autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to width 2800 (folio101: 2200), and UnsharpMask radius 1, percent 80, threshold 3; rotation was zero.

The opening is a continuation beginning morphismes de normalisation. No material from another page was read or supplied to complete it. The long dash after normalisation is retained; C and H differ there only in its TeX encoding.

The writer revises isomorphismes to above-line équivalences twice. Both strikes and both replacement attachments are clear, but hidden letters under each strike remain locally doubtful. The short deleted multi candidate is retained separately before live groupoïdes.

The opening transf/full-transforme alternatives and the later automatiq with raised t/full-automatiquement alternatives remain unresolved. No abbreviation stop is added. They are not counted as errors against a witness whose full form remains admitted.

The m.graphes term has a low m and a separately visible stop on this leaf. It is recovered from H's illegible marker. This observation does not settle whether similarly small stops are separate on any other page.

The comparison in (144) literally has two waves over a straight bar and is represented by approxeq. Both Pi symbols in this display have the numeral index 1. The product is indexed by alpha in S; its right-hand M term retains the locally doubtful first letter, the comma, the hatted I-alpha and the sole visible closing parenthesis.

The first subscript in (144) is visibly reworked, but no recoverable old/new letter sequence is asserted. H's editorial description of rewriting is not additional source text. The cancelled raised group is retained with a tentative star; H acknowledges that group in an editorial note, so its uncertain content is not counted as a settled H omission.

The inserted de belongs after compte and before the opening parenthesis around et redonne and its adverb. The drawn placement guide is treated as part of the insertion attachment, not as a letter or an independent mathematical sign. Les begins the following baseline outside that parenthesis.

The inline Pi-M connection has no numeral index 1, unlike both Pi terms in (144). Its graph indices are G-prime at the left and G at the right. The connector endpoint remains local doubt; the complete formula is included in its crop and blind box.

The writer claims that the operation under discussion sends strict normalisation morphisms to equivalences of groupoids and sums of stable m.graphes to products of the corresponding groupoids. The page then presents (144) as the principal formula. These are the author's statements, not independently verified results of this reading.

The normalisés parenthesis names tilde-G-prime and tilde-G de G, exactly as written. The last unprimed G is not silently changed to fit an expected symmetric phrase. The source then gives square (145), with tilded upper objects, primed left objects, and four single directed arrows.

Square (145) was checked object by object and arrow by arrow. Both horizontal connectors have visible rightward heads and both vertical connectors have downward heads. No arrow label, diagonal, doubled shaft, additional object or cancellation is established within the square.

Two minute dark spots between (145) and the square and one minute spot beside the upper-right G do not establish meaningful pen marks. They are noted as unassigned specks and are not promoted to punctuation, a prime or extra diagram objects. No genuine drawing is identified elsewhere on this leaf.

The final paragraph states a strictness criterion using the corresponding morphism on the normalisés (totaux), ending with the singly underlined abbreviation iso and a three-point ellipsis before the closing parenthesis. The connector and terminal s remain doubtful. The criterion was not independently proved or used to force those readings.
Manuscript page number 50 is written at the top. Pale foliation 101 is written at the lower-left edge. No named-hand attribution is assigned to the paler foliation.

The report contains eleven substantive correction places: three against C and nine against H, with the comparison-sign correction shared. Unresolved word endings, covered cancelled letters, g/G, the cancelled exponent, connector subtype refinements and the final s are not counted as settled witness errors.

The blind boxes cover every insertion and cancellation, all word differences, all assigned marks, all below-high-confidence departures from C, the complete doubtful formulas and diagram, and every numeral group: page 50, formula 144, both Pi indices 1, formula 145 and foliation 101. Boundaries combine adjoining prose where needed to avoid clipping cross-line strokes. No OCR, external research or TeX compilation was performed.
